clock: presentation seconds per phase only; no shared biological rate

voltage.title: Membrane voltage propagation
voltage.scope: Presentation cursor marks local current and nodal regeneration. It is not a moving cargo particle or a measured propagation recording.

phases.label: Initial segment trigger
phases.detail: Integrated depolarization can initiate an action potential at the axon initial segment; no vesicle has to travel the axon for each spike.

phases.label: Internodal current
phases.detail: Local electrical current spreads under myelin; it is not a leap of the membrane itself across empty space.

phases.label: Next exposed node
phases.detail: Voltage-gated channels at a node regenerate the action potential. Axon diameter, myelin and temperature affect speed.

phases.label: Terminal arrival
phases.detail: Terminal depolarization can open voltage-gated calcium channels before transmitter release. Detailed excitability follows in the next chapter.

cargo.title: Physical axonal cargo traffic
cargo.scope: The cursor follows representative tracks, not a single molecule or measured trajectory; kinesin/dynein labels are cargo-specific exemplars.

phases.label: Soma sorting
phases.detail: Transcription makes mRNA; ribosomes translate selected proteins. Sorting/loading need not imply DNA replication, and some local axonal translation occurs.

phases.label: Anterograde delivery
phases.detail: Plus-end-directed kinesin-family motors carry selected cargo toward distal axon on polarized microtubules.

phases.label: Terminal use and recycling
phases.detail: Cargo may be used, recycled locally or enter endosomal pathways; not every transmitter molecule returns to the soma.

phases.label: Retrograde signaling
phases.detail: Minus-end-directed dynein–dynactin carries selected endosomes and organelles toward the soma; this includes some injury signals.

injury.title: Injury classes: compare structures
injury.scope: These are alternative classes, not successive states of one injured axon. Seeking changes the comparison row.

phases.label: Neurapraxia
phases.detail: Axonal continuity is preserved; local conduction block may involve myelin. Distal Wallerian axon degeneration does not follow from this class.

phases.label: Axonotmesis
phases.detail: Axon is interrupted; distal Wallerian degeneration follows. Connective guidance may be preserved to differing Sunderland degrees.

phases.label: Neurotmesis
phases.detail: Complete nerve disruption includes axon and guidance structures in the canonical class; distal Wallerian degeneration follows.

repair.title: Conditional peripheral repair sequence
repair.scope: A conceptual axon-disconnection branch. Presentation seconds do not map to days, growth rate, remyelination rate or functional recovery.

phases.label: Proximal survival
phases.detail: A viable cell body and its proximal stump are prerequisites for extension from that neuron; proximal retraction can coexist with distal breakdown.

phases.label: Distal Wallerian change
phases.detail: Disconnected distal axon and myelin fragment; degeneration is not a neurapraxia event.

phases.label: Repair-cell response
phases.detail: Schwann cells change state, organize guidance tracks and cooperate with macrophages in debris clearance. Mouse c-Jun evidence is mechanistic, not a human timetable.

phases.label: Proximal sprout
phases.detail: New extension arises from the surviving proximal neuron into a permissive path; alignment, distance and target viability matter.

phases.label: Later distinct outcomes
phases.detail: Remyelination and target-specific reconnection are separate from axon extension; neither guarantees normal function.
